hook_text: The bus timetable says the last bus leaves at 21:40. Is that a.m., p.m., or a typo?
clip_script: Nomsa's day in Pietermaritzburg. Alarm: short hand just past 6, long hand on the 3. Count the minutes in fives: 15. It is 6:15 a.m. School ends at half past one in the afternoon: 1:30 p.m. Now the bus timetable uses the 24-hour way. No a.m., no p.m., the hours count all the way to 23. After midday, add 12. 1:30 p.m. is 13:30. Bedtime 8:30 p.m. is 20:30. So 21:40? Take away 12: 9:40 p.m. Not a typo, just the last bus at night. Two ways to write time, one day.
visual_style: Whiteboard clock face with hands moving through Nomsa's day; a digital display flipping between 12-hour and 24-hour times; a bus timetable with 21:40 circled.
pacing: The timetable puzzle, the clock reading, the add-12 rule, then the answer.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write your own day in both the 12-hour and the 24-hour way.
